rows.rationale: Cites AU-specific formatting and clear fields: phone helpText 'Include country code if you are calling from outside Australia' and phone placeholder '+61 4xx xxx xxx', plus an email field with placeholder '[SCRUBBED_EMAIL]' and full T-shirt options (XS..XXL). Weakness: no explicit consent/terms or validation patterns for required fields, so validation intent scored lower.

Includes Sydney-specific copy and structure: page title 'Annual Sales Conference — Sydney Registration' and paragraph text referencing Sydney, phone placeholder '+61 4XX XXX XXX', and checkbox dietary options including 'Other (please specify at check-in)'. Weakness: lacks explicit consent/marketing terms and uses an offline 'specify at check-in' option that weakens online validation and copy quality.

Contains clear US-centric artifacts despite AU audience: a phone helpText explicitly instructs 'start with +1' and there is a 'ZIP code' field with placeholder 'ZIP / postal code'. Strength: all requested fields present (phone, email, ZIP, t-shirt, dietary, terms). Weakness: severe cross-locale leakage (ZIP and +1) that reduces locale fidelity, validation accuracy, and cultural register.

Well-aligned AU RSVP: phone placeholder '+61 4xx xxx xxx', session-choice radio ('Keynote & Plenary', 'Data Science Workshop' etc.), and an explicit consent terms label 'I agree to receive event updates and marketing communications...'. Weakness: consent text bundles marketing and updates without a separate opt-out granularly explained, so policy compliance isn't perfect.

Sydney-specific RSVP with clear elements: paragraph label 'Location: Sydney', session dropdown options and 'Consent to receive event updates' terms component. Weakness: one small copy gap — phone and email placeholders are generic ('[SCRUBBED_PHONE]','[SCRUBBED_EMAIL]') which lowers copy polish slightly compared to more explicit local formatting.
